segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Praise of salvation to the Lord.
After Deborah and Barak, the Midianites [ruled] seven (7)
years tyrannical sway over the people,
until Gideon destroyed them.
[Af]ter the Midianites, Gideon judged the people forty years.
And to Gideon were born seventy sons.
And at that time Apollo reigned in Thebes, he who by the song of his lyre, they say, used to entice stones,
that is to say, heavy and tyrannical hearts.
[After Gi]deon, Abimelech his son,
the one who was born of a concubine.
And when he killed his seventy brothers,
he judged the people three years.
After Abimelech, Tola, twenty years.
And in his twentieth year,
the city of Tarsus was built by Perseus son of Danae.
And Carthage was also built.
And Ilion was conquered;
others say that it was conquered in the days of Samson.
After Tola, Jair the Gileadite judged the people twenty-two years.
After Jair, the [Ammon]ites {OCR?} ruled tyrannically over the Hebrews eighteen years,
and greatly oppressed the Hebrews,
until they were defeated by Jephthah.
[Jeph]thah, six years.
And those who say twenty-four,
join with them the eighteen of the Ammonites.
Therefore, when the Hebrews were being greatly oppressed by the Ammonites,
the inhabitants of Gilead went to Jephthah, after they had driven him away from them,
and brought him,
and he became their chief.
He who, when he fought and was victorious,
offered his daughter as a sacrifice,
according to his vow, which is not commendable.
[After Jeph]thah, seven years.
Some of the chroniclers do not mention this name at all.
After Ibzan, Elon the Zebulunite, ten years.
John of Yathrib, however, says seven.
And this [man] is not in the Septuagint translation.
And after [E]lon, Abdon, eight years.
And in the seventh year of this Abdon,
there arose the first king of the Latins,
that is to say, the Romans, who are the Franks:
Aeneas,
three years,
and according to others, eight.
After Abdon, the Philistines ruled tyrannically over the people forty years,
which Eusebius does not include.
Annianos, however, sets down forty,
and Andronicus says twenty only.
[Samson the] Nazirite,
from the tribe of Dan,
judged the people twenty [years]. 16
